claims.title: Cancel All Federal Student Debt
claims.socialistClaimText: Federal student loans are a trap sold as opportunity. Wipe the entire federal student-debt book so a generation can buy homes, start families, and stop paying tribute to the Department of Education.
claims.executiveSummary: Balances are large, and some programs failed borrowers. Federal Student Aid, Treasury Fiscal Data, and NCES already publish outstanding federal loans, originations, and attainment. Cancellation is a transfer to people who already received the tuition, not a refund of the classroom. It does not lower the next cohort's sticker price. Schools that captured the loans keep the buildings. Taxpayers who did not attend, or who already repaid, fund the wipe. Pause-and-forgive cycles also reprice the next origination. The unseen half is tuition that keeps rising after the slate is clean.
evidenceBullets: FSA Federal Student Loan Portfolio pages report outstanding Direct, FFEL, and Perkins balances by status. A slogan wipe is not an inventory.
Treasury Federal Borrowings Program tables track agency credit as loans receivable. Cancellation is a fiscal event, not a free lunch.
NCES Fast Facts on tuition still publish sticker prices and attainment. Debt cancellation does not write those series down.
Borrowers who already repaid, and households that never borrowed, are the residual payers unless taxes or other outlays fall.

claims.title: Ban Junk Fees So the Sticker Is the Price
claims.socialistClaimText: Airlines, landlords, tickets, and banks hide the real price in junk fees. Ban surprise add-ons so the advertised number is what you pay, and stop firms from nickel-and-diming households.
claims.executiveSummary: Opaque add-ons are a real consumer-protection problem, and CFPB, FTC, and BLS already police deception and measure prices. A total ban on optional paid extras is not the same as requiring the all-in number up front. Unbundling can be a feature: a bag fee lets a traveler who packs light pay less. If every add-on is illegal, the base sticker rises and the option disappears. Truth-in-advertising and itemized checkout are the narrow tools. A slogan ban on fees is a price control on a menu of services.
evidenceBullets: CFPB junk-fees policy pages treat surprise, unavoidable add-ons as a disclosure and unfairness problem, not a proof that every optional fee is theft.
The FTC 2024 Junk Fees Rule (tickets and short-term lodging) requires advertised total price including mandatory fees. It does not ban optional add-ons or any specific fee amount.
BLS CPI baskets include fees that households actually pay. A ban that forces bundling changes the index composition, it does not freeze real resource cost.
An optional fee that some buyers skip is a price. Forbidding it transfers the cost into the base fare.

claims.title: Make Childcare a Public Utility
claims.socialistClaimText: Childcare is too expensive because markets ration care. Make it a free public utility like kindergarten so parents can work and children get equal starts.
claims.executiveSummary: Prices are high in many metros, and quality is uneven. Census, BLS, and HHS/ACF already measure who uses paid care, what it costs, and how subsidies work. Turning care into a free utility is a labor-demand shock for workers who currently do the job, plus a fiscal commitment that does not create extra classrooms overnight. Waiting lists, staffing ratios, and facility rules still bind. Countries that expanded public slots did not abolish scarcity; they reassigned who waits and who pays. Parental time is still a real input.
evidenceBullets: Census child-care pages document arrangements, costs, and which households use paid care versus relatives.
BLS Occupational Outlook: childcare workers, 2025 median pay $34,980, about 1.0 million jobs. A 'free utility' still has to hire them at a wage.
HHS Office of Child Care administers existing subsidy and quality programs. Scaling to universal free slots is a different budget, not a missing office.
Capacity, ratios, and background-check rules are quantity constraints. Zero price does not add rooms.

claims.title: Ban Private Prisons
claims.socialistClaimText: Private prisons profit from cages. Ban them so incarceration cannot be a business and the state stops filling beds for contractors.
claims.executiveSummary: Contractor incentives are a real governance issue, and BJS, BOP, and Census of Governments already count who holds prisoners and who pays. Most U.S. inmates sit in public facilities. A ban on private operators shifts the same bodies onto state payrolls; it does not repeal sentencing statutes or crime. Occupancy guarantees in some contracts are the narrow scandal. Ending those clauses is not the same as pretending public guards have no overtime, no unions, and no budget incentive to keep capacity. The crime and sentencing book is the volume knob.
evidenceBullets: BJS Prisoners in 2023: 88,600 persons (7.1% of jurisdiction) were in privately operated prisons. Most custody is public. FBOP reported no prisoners in secure private prisons.
Federal BOP pages document federal custody, contracts, and facility lists. A slogan ban is not a sentencing reform.
Census of Governments tracks state and local correctional employment and spending. Public systems are already a large payroll.
Bed volume follows convictions and sentence length. Changing the contractor does not change the docket.

claims.title: Ban Congress from Trading Stocks
claims.socialistClaimText: Members of Congress write the rules and then trade the companies they regulate. Ban individual stock trading so the rich in office cannot front-run the public.
claims.executiveSummary: Conflict of interest is a real ethics problem, and House, Senate, and SEC already run disclosure and insider-trading law. A total ban on individual names is one instrument; index funds, blind trusts, and enforcement of the STOCK Act are others. Most household wealth is not a member's ticker tape. Banning members from diversified funds can shrink the talent pool without proving committee votes were purchased. The narrow fix is timely disclosure and prosecution of actual material nonpublic information. A slogan ban is not a substitute for reading the ethics filings.
evidenceBullets: House Ethics publishes STOCK Act and financial-disclosure rules for members and staff.
Senate Ethics covers the same duty in the Senate. The paperwork already exists; late filings are an enforcement fact.
SEC insider-trading and reporting pages apply to anyone who trades on material nonpublic information, including officials.
A ban that forbids even broad index funds treats diversified beta as a crime. That is a different claim from stopping a committee chair's single-name flip.

claims.title: Ban Payday Loans
claims.socialistClaimText: Payday lenders trap the working poor in triple-digit APR cycles. Ban the product so households cannot be harvested by storefront credit.
claims.executiveSummary: High APRs on short loans are ugly, and CFPB, FDIC, and the Fed already publish how these products work and who uses them. A ban removes one expensive option. It does not create a cheap unsecured substitute for a bounced rent check. Informal lenders, overdraft, and bounced-check fees are the usual substitutes. Usury caps that kill legal storefronts historically push volume off-book. Disclosure, ability-to-repay, and bank small-dollar products are narrower tools. Pretending zero price credit appears after a ban is the free-lunch step.
evidenceBullets: CFPB payday-loan consumer tools describe typical terms, rollovers, and complaint patterns.
FDIC 2023 National Survey: 14.2% of U.S. households were underbanked, including use of payday and other nonbank credit. A ban does not create a cheap substitute.
Federal Reserve consumer and community pages cover small-dollar credit and overdraft as neighboring products.
A ban that closes legal storefronts does not close the rent due date. Substitution is the unseen half.

claims.title: Forgive All Medical Debt
claims.socialistClaimText: Nobody should go bankrupt from a hospital bill. Wipe medical debt from credit reports and cancel outstanding balances so illness is not a collections industry.
claims.executiveSummary: Medical bills wreck some households, and CFPB, CMS, and Census already measure spending, insurance, and collections. Forgiving today's balances is a transfer to providers and borrowers on the existing stock. It does not set tomorrow's chargemaster or insurance design. Credit-report removal is a scoring change; cancellation is a fiscal or hospital-writeoff event. If prices and utilization stay the same, the next cohort re-accumulates the same book. Narrower tools are price transparency, emergency-care rules, and insurance. A one-time wipe is not a cost curve.
evidenceBullets: CFPB credit-report research: medical collections are about half of collections tradelines. Later bureau changes still left millions with medical bills on file. A wipe is not a cost curve.
CMS National Health Expenditure data remain the official U.S. health-spending accounts. Debt is a lagging claim on that spending.
Census health-insurance and household pages show coverage gaps that generate uncompensated and delayed bills.
Wiping yesterday's receivables does not bind tomorrow's list prices or utilization.

claims.title: Ban Stock Buybacks
claims.socialistClaimText: Buybacks starve workers and investment so executives can juice the ticker. Ban share repurchases and force profits into wages and factories.
claims.executiveSummary: Repurchases return cash to owners, and SEC, BEA, and Treasury already measure corporate profits, distributions, and buyback disclosure. A ban does not create a wage fund. Cash that cannot be returned via buybacks still belongs to residual claimants: dividends, cash piles, M&A, or debt paydown. Investment happens when projects beat the cost of capital, not when a distribution channel is closed. Workers are paid from product markets and labor markets. Treating a ticker-support tool as the reason real wages stall skips productivity and labor supply. Disclosure of 10b-18 programs is the narrow governance tool.
evidenceBullets: SEC Item 703 still requires periodic repurchase disclosure. The 2023 daily-disclosure modernization rule was vacated in Chamber of Commerce v. SEC; disclosure reverted to the prior Item 703 regime.
BEA corporate profits from current production are a NIPA income flow, separate from dividends and investment. Closing one distribution channel does not create a wage fund.
Federal Reserve Z.1 Financial Accounts record corporate equity issuance and buybacks as financial transactions, not payroll.
If a project has a positive NPV, firms can fund it with retained earnings or new capital whether or not buybacks exist.
